title: Cohort-driven introspective calibrator for AWQ/GPTQ quant profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run targeted evaluation sweeps that couple per-layer sensitivity measurements with cohort-level fidelity metrics to automatically recommend int8/int4 profile thresholds for AWQ and GPTQ conversions. The goal is to produce a conservative, explainable thresholding heuristic that minimizes semantic regressions (measured by a mix of likelihood, n-gram and embedding-based metrics) while preserving cost and latency gains. This ticket builds the harness, defines cohorts, runs the sweep, and surfaces recommendations into the Console gating dashboard and alerting system.
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can run AWQ and GPTQ conversion on a given model+checkpoint and produce a per-layer sensitivity report in under 6 hours for a 13B model on the standard bench infra.
Threshold recommender outputs a ranked list of profile candidates (int8/int4) with estimated semantic delta, 95% confidence interval, and expected token-cost delta.
Console gating dashboard shows the recommended threshold and an explanation bundle (top-5 sensitive layers, cohort breakdown) and links to the full eval results.
If a recommended profile's estimated semantic delta exceeds the configured alert threshold, an automated 'soft-block' is emitted to the rollout pipeline (canary fails with advisory).
steps_taken: Defined 6 evaluation cohorts: general chat, code-gen, summarization, instruction-following, multi-turn dialogue, and safety-stress tests.
Implemented per-layer perturbation harness that applies AWQ/GPTQ conversions per-layer and measures metric deltas without full-retrain runs (fast approximation).

Instrumented semantic metrics: token-level logprob delta, BLEU-style n-gram recall for code/summaries, embedding cosine (model-embedding) drift using S-BERT baseline, and a calibrated human-like acceptability proxy derived from previous evals.
Built a ROC-like threshold selector that trades off semantic delta vs cost/latency reduction. Initial selector implemented as Pareto frontier + preferred operating point heuristic.
Wired outputs into a staging Console dashboard (private link) and added trace IDs to link back to conversion jobs and PRs.
results_summary: Early runs on small set of 13B models show AWQ-int8 profiles produce median embedding cosine 0.984 vs FP16 baseline on general chat but 0.96 on code-gen cohort; GPTQ-int4 aggressive profiles show larger variance on multi-turn dialogue with occasional token-level logprob regressions > 1.2 nats for rare tokens. The recommender flags a small set of layers (decoder blocks 20-24) as high-sensitivity for code-gen and multi-turn cohorts. Cost projections indicate a 28-35% token-cost reduction for accepted int8 profiles and up to 55% for int4 if applied selectively by cohort.
next_steps: Run full sweep across our standard model catalog (small/medium/13B/70B) to collect statistics and refine percentile-based thresholds.
Add a lightweight human evaluation pass for top candidate profiles on the code-gen cohort (3 raters per example) to validate acceptability proxy.
Prototype an automated gating rule in rollout service: if predicted semantic delta > 0.015 embedding cosine or logprob shift > 0.8 nats then block auto-rollout and surface advisory to SRE/PM.
Optimize per-layer AWQ conversion runtime to reduce end-to-end sweep time by ~2x (profiling indicates quant kernel packing is the hotspot).
Coordinate with Console team to add a drill-down that shows per-cohort histograms and layer heatmaps for each candidate profile.
